misclassified_entities.reason: A calling contract is another smart contract within the same EVM execution context. While it may be untrusted code, it is not an external entity crossing a trust boundary - it operates within the same execution environment.

The blob transaction is the source of data, but by the time the precompile is called, the transaction has already been validated and included in a block. The actual external boundary is at transaction submission, not precompile invocation.
This is a potential victim contract, not an entity sending data into the system. It represents the impact target of attacks, not a trust boundary crossing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain Consensus Layer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The beacon chain provides RANDAO values to the execution layer. It is semi-trusted because: (1) validators collectively contribute to RANDAO, (2) individual proposers can bias by 1 bit, (3) the execution-consensus interface is assumed secure. The beacon chain is under Ethereum's overall governance but individual values can be influenced.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer Validator
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The validator proposing a block controls the RANDAO reveal and can choose to skip slots to influence randomness. Proposers are authenticated via validator keys but their intent is not trusted - they may attempt to bias outcomes for profit.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Block Proposer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Threat model entity representing a validator willing to sacrifice block rewards to bias RANDAO. Explicitly models the adversarial capability of 1-bit influence per controlled slot.

trusted_external_entities.name: EIP Proposal Author
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Community member or developer submitting EIP proposals. No authentication required for proposal submission. Proposals must go through review process. Authors could submit malicious or poorly designed proposals.

trusted_external_entities.name: Client Development Teams
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Ethereum client teams (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon, etc.) coordinate activation times. Teams are known entities with established track records. However, coordination failures are possible. Trust is based on reputation and governance process.

trusted_external_entities.name: Withdrawal Credential Owner
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EOA or smart contract holding 0x01 withdrawal credentials for a validator. Authenticated via Ethereum address matching validator's registered credentials. Intent is semi-trusted - owner may legitimately withdraw or may be compromised.

trusted_external_entities.name: Withdrawal Contract Caller
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External caller invoking the withdrawal predeploy contract. No authentication at execution layer - any address can call. Authorization is verified at consensus layer by matching source_address to validator credentials.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (PoW Miner)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Proof-of-work miner producing blocks with difficulty calculation. Miners are anonymous participants. Blocks must be fully validated including difficulty value. Miners could attempt to manipulate timestamps to affect difficulty.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peer transmitting blocks for validation. Anonymous network participant. All block data including stated difficulty must be independently validated. Peers could send blocks with invalid difficulty.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: RANDAO values from beacon chain are authentic but biasable. Execution clients retrieve values via trusted consensus-execution interface. Applications should not rely on RANDAO for high-stakes immediate randomness.
Proposer contributes to RANDAO via reveal. Proposer can bias by 1 bit by choosing to skip slot. Cost is forfeited block rewards. Multi-epoch delay required for unpredictable randomness.
EIP proposals are reviewed by core developers. Technical merit evaluated before inclusion. Malicious proposals filtered through governance process. No direct code execution from proposal submission.

Client teams coordinate via public channels (AllCoreDevs). Activation times must be consistent across all clients. Misconfiguration risk exists - different teams could set different times causing chain splits.

Withdrawal credential owner is authorized to trigger validator exits/withdrawals. Consensus layer validates source_address matches validator's 0x01 credentials. Custody arrangements may rely on this mechanism.
Any address can call withdrawal predeploy. Input must be exactly 56 bytes for request or 0 bytes for fee query. Authorization deferred to consensus layer credential validation.

Miners produce blocks requiring difficulty calculation. Post-fork blocks use adjusted formula with 11.4M offset. Difficulty must be validated against expected value. Timestamp manipulation limited by protocol rules.
Peers propagate blocks that must be independently validated. Stated difficulty must match calculated expected difficulty. Blocks with incorrect difficulty are rejected.
